provenance.fixture: dataset_monstree/mini6 (configuration above, enforced by the runner). The global mapper stage invokes each COLMAP binary's `global_mapper` command directly; extraction and matching are the same seeded SIFT stages as the incremental gate.
provenance.rule: Count metrics are discrete, so any difference is algorithmic and the threshold is 0. Each continuous threshold is the log-space midpoint sqrt(lower_input * upper_input), rounded to one significant digit. It is never fitted to the candidate.

lower_input.method: The measured cross-binary divergence is the effective noise floor of this comparison: three repeated runs of both binaries were bit-identical per side (candidate model sha bd86dc20ff4d9edf, baseline 2f9a3624c1557c3c over images.txt+points3D.txt), so the fork/upstream delta below is stable and reproducible, not run noise
lower_input.notes: The rotation delta was measured as exactly 0, so the acos resolution near identity (acos(1 - 2^-53) = 8.5e-7 deg) is used as the lower input.

smallest_algorithmic_divergence.method: Upper input = smallest real algorithmic perturbation measured on this fixture (incremental pipeline, std::unordered hash containers versus upstream boost::unordered 1.92, i.e. SfM gauge and BA residual-order divergence). A real global-pipeline regression is expected at or above this scale; the observed global-pipeline fork/upstream deltas sit 4-7 decades below it

provenance.scope: Same-host gate only. A different CPU, compiler, or BLAS can move the floating-point floor and requires re-measuring both inputs of the rule.
